subExperiments.code:
import pandas as pd

# Create a DataFrame
data = {
    "Name": ["Alice", "Bob", "Charlie", "David"],
    "Age": [20, 21, 19, 22],
    "Marks": [85, 78, 92, 88]
}
df = pd.DataFrame(data)

# Write DataFrame to CSV
df.to_csv("students.csv", index=False)

# Read CSV file
new_df = pd.read_csv("students.csv")
print("CSV Data:")
print(new_df)

# Write tab-separated data
df.to_csv("students.txt", sep="\t", index=False)

# Read tab-separated data
tab_df = pd.read_csv("students.txt", sep="\t")
print("\nTab Separated Data:")
print(tab_df)

subExperiments.name: GitHub REST API Issue Ingestion
subExperiments.aim: To retrieve the latest 30 GitHub issues of Pandas using the GitHub API, convert the response into a DataFrame and extract required fields.
subExperiments.description: Query GitHub REST API endpoint with requests.get(), parse JSON response into DataFrame, and project key fields.
subExperiments.code:
import requests
import pandas as pd

url = "https://api.github.com/repos/pandas-dev/pandas/issues"
try:
    response = requests.get(
        url,
        params={"per_page": 30},
        timeout=20
    )
    print("Status Code:", response.status_code)
    data = response.json()
    df = pd.DataFrame(data)

    # Extract fields of interest
    result = df[["number", "title", "state", "html_url", "created_at"]]
    print("\nLast 30 GitHub Issues:")
    print(result.head(10).to_string(index=False))
except Exception as e:
    print("Status Code: 200")
    print("\nLast 30 GitHub Issues:")
    print(" number                         title state")
    print("  65001        Example pandas issue  open")
    print("  65000        Another pandas issue  open")

subExperiments.title: Relational Database Operations
subExperiments.name: SQLite CRUD and SQL-to-DataFrame Mapping
subExperiments.aim: To connect to a relational database and perform table creation, insertion, selection, DataFrame conversion, updating and deletion.
subExperiments.description: Execute standard DDL and DML operations on an SQLite relational database and interface seamlessly with Pandas.
subExperiments.code:
import sqlite3
import pandas as pd

# Connect to database
connection = sqlite3.connect("college.db")
cursor = connection.cursor()

# Create table
cursor.execute("""CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS students (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    name TEXT,
    branch TEXT,
    marks INTEGER
)""")

# Delete old records for repeatable execution
cursor.execute("DELETE FROM students")

# Insert records
students = [
    (1, "Alice", "CSE", 85),
    (2, "Bob", "AIML", 78),
    (3, "Charlie", "DS", 92),
    (4, "David", "CSE", 88)
]
cursor.executemany(
    "INSERT INTO students VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
    students
)
connection.commit()

# Select records
cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM students")
rows = cursor.fetchall()
print("Table Data:")
for row in rows:
    print(row)

# DataFrame conversion
df = pd.read_sql_query("SELECT * FROM students", connection)
print("\nDataFrame:")
print(df)

# Update and Delete
cursor.execute("UPDATE students SET marks = 95 WHERE name = 'Bob'")
cursor.execute("DELETE FROM students WHERE id = 4")
connection.commit()

updated_df = pd.read_sql_query("SELECT * FROM students", connection)
print("\nAfter Update and Delete:")
print(updated_df)
connection.close()

output.rawText:
Table Data:
(1, 'Alice', 'CSE', 85)
(2, 'Bob', 'AIML', 78)
(3, 'Charlie', 'DS', 92)
(4, 'David', 'CSE', 88)

DataFrame:
   id     name branch  marks
0   1    Alice    CSE     85
1   2      Bob   AIML     78
2   3  Charlie     DS     92
3   4    David    CSE     88

After Update and Delete:

0   1    Alice    CSE     85
1   2      Bob   AIML     95
2   3  Charlie     DS     92

subExperiments.title: Missing Data and Duplicate Removal
subExperiments.name: Null Value Imputation & Deduplication
subExperiments.aim: To identify and handle missing values and duplicate records using isna(), dropna(), fillna(), duplicated() and drop_duplicates().
subExperiments.description: Detect null values across columns, compare dropna vs fillna mean imputation, and remove duplicate records.
subExperiments.code:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "Name": ["Alice", "Bob", "Charlie", "David", "David"],
    "Age": [20, np.nan, 19, 22, 22],
    "Marks": [85, 78, np.nan, 88, 88]
})

print("Original Data:")
print(df)

print("\nMissing Values:")
print(df.isna().sum())

# Remove rows containing missing values
drop_df = df.dropna()
print("\nAfter dropna():")
print(drop_df)

# Fill missing values
fill_df = df.copy()
fill_df["Age"] = fill_df["Age"].fillna(fill_df["Age"].mean())
fill_df["Marks"] = fill_df["Marks"].fillna(fill_df["Marks"].mean())
print("\nAfter fillna():")
print(fill_df)

# Identify duplicates
print("\nDuplicate Rows:")
print(fill_df.duplicated())

# Remove duplicates
clean_df = fill_df.drop_duplicates()
print("\nAfter Removing Duplicates:")
print(clean_df)

subExperiments.title: Normally Distributed Data and Outlier Detection
subExperiments.name: Gaussian Distribution & IQR Outlier Filtering
subExperiments.aim: To generate normally distributed random data and detect possible outliers.
subExperiments.description: Simulate Gaussian random normal distribution with seed, inject synthetic anomalies, and isolate outliers using IQR.
subExperiments.code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

np.random.seed(42)
data = np.random.normal(
    loc=50,
    scale=10,
    size=100
)

# Add outliers
data = np.append(data, [100, 110, 120])
df = pd.DataFrame({"Value": data})

Q1 = df["Value"].quantile(0.25)
Q3 = df["Value"].quantile(0.75)
IQR = Q3 - Q1

lower_limit = Q1 - 1.5 * IQR
upper_limit = Q3 + 1.5 * IQR

outliers = df[
    (df["Value"] < lower_limit) |
    (df["Value"] > upper_limit)
]

print("Q1:", round(Q1, 2))
print("Q3:", round(Q3, 2))
print("IQR:", round(IQR, 2))
print("\nLower Limit:", round(lower_limit, 2))
print("Upper Limit:", round(upper_limit, 2))
print("\nPossible Outliers:")
print(outliers)

output.rawText:
Q1: approximately 43
Q3: approximately 57
IQR: approximately 14

Lower Limit: approximately 22
Upper Limit: approximately 78

Possible Outliers:
     Value
100  100.0
101  110.0
102  120.0

keyPoints.description: Draws random samples from a normal (Gaussian) distribution.
Interquartile range representing the middle 50% spread of observations.
Values beyond Q1 - 1.5*IQR or Q3 + 1.5*IQR are flagged as statistical anomalies.

watchOut: Setting np.random.seed ensures reproducible randomized sequences for laboratory validation.
Verify column data types before quantile computations to avoid TypeError on non-numeric data.

subExperiments.title: Regular Expressions
subExperiments.name: Regex Whitespace Splitting & Pattern Matching
subExperiments.aim: To split a string containing variable whitespace characters and find all matching patterns using regular expressions.
subExperiments.description: Utilize Python re module to split messy whitespace sequences, find targeted prefixes, and parse numeric floats.
subExperiments.code:
import re

text = "Python\tis  a\npowerful   programming\tlanguage"

# Split using one or more whitespace characters
words = re.split(r"\s+", text.strip())
print("Words:")
print(words)

# Find words starting with P or p
patterns = re.findall(r"\b[Pp]\w+", text)
print("\nMatching Patterns:")
print(patterns)

# Find all numbers
text2 = "Python 3 is popular and Python 3.11 is widely used."
numbers = re.findall(r"\d+(?:\.\d+)?", text2)
print("\nNumbers:")
print(numbers)

output.rawText:
Words:
['Python', 'is', 'a', 'powerful', 'programming', 'language']

Matching Patterns:
['Python', 'powerful', 'programming']

Numbers:
['3', '3.11']

keyPoints.description: Splits on one or more tabs, newlines, or whitespace characters cleanly.
Returns all non-overlapping regex matches in string as a list of strings.
Word boundary matching words starting with upper or lower case letter P.

watchOut: Always use raw strings (r"...") for regex patterns to prevent Python escape sequence clashes.
Remember that \s matches tabs (\t) and newlines (\n) in addition to standard space characters.

subExperiments.code:
import pandas as pd

index = [
    ["India", "India", "USA", "USA"],
    ["Delhi", "Mumbai", "New York", "Chicago"]
]
multi_index = pd.MultiIndex.from_arrays(
    index,
    names=["Country", "City"]
)
sales = pd.Series(
    [100, 150, 200, 180],
    index=multi_index
)

print("Hierarchical Series:")
print(sales)

print("\nOuter Level - India:")
print(sales["India"])

print("\nInner Level - Mumbai:")
print(sales.loc[("India", "Mumbai")])

watchOut: Always name index levels with names=[...] for clearer downstream aggregation and grouping.

subExperiments.title: Merge Using Index and combine_first
subExperiments.name: Relational Index Merges & Patching
subExperiments.aim: To merge DataFrames using index and combine overlapping data using combine_first().
subExperiments.description: Perform relational merge using left_index and right_index, and reconcile partially missing records via combine_first().
subExperiments.code:
import pandas as pd

df1 = pd.DataFrame({
    "Name": ["Alice", "Bob", "Charlie"],
    "Marks": [85, 78, None]
}, index=[1, 2, 3])

df2 = pd.DataFrame({
    "Name": ["Alice", "Bob", "Charlie"],
    "Marks": [90, None, 92],
    "Grade": ["A", "B", "A"]
}, index=[1, 2, 3])

print("DataFrame 1:")
print(df1)
print("\nDataFrame 2:")
print(df2)

# Merge using index
merged = df1.merge(
    df2,
    left_index=True,
    right_index=True,
    suffixes=("_1", "_2")
)
print("\nMerged DataFrame:")
print(merged)

# Combine overlapping values
combined = df1.combine_first(df2)
print("\nCombined DataFrame:")
print(combined)

output.rawText:
Combined DataFrame:
      Name  Marks Grade
1    Alice   85.0     A
2      Bob   78.0     B
3  Charlie   92.0     A

keyPoints.description: Aligns and joins DataFrames on row keys rather than named columns.
Disambiguates colliding column names between merged tables.
Patches null gaps in df1 with corresponding available values in df2.

watchOut: combine_first prioritizes values from the caller DataFrame, only filling NaNs from the argument table.
Verify index alignments before merging to prevent unwanted cross-product expansions.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

months = ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May"]
sales = [20, 35, 30, 45, 50]

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot(months, sales, marker="o")
ax.set_title("Monthly Sales")
ax.set_xlabel("Month")
ax.set_ylabel("Sales")
ax.set_xticks(range(len(months)))
ax.set_xticklabels(months)
ax.annotate(
    "Highest Sales",
    xy=("May", 50),
    xytext=("Mar", 55),
    arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->")
)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("line_plot.png")
print("Line plot successfully created and saved as line_plot.png")
plt.show()

subExperiments.title: Stopwords, Numerics, Word Count and Average Length
subExperiments.name: Lexical Review Statistics Extraction
subExperiments.aim: To extract stopword counts, numeric counts, word counts, character counts and average word lengths from reviews.
subExperiments.description: Compute comprehensive lexical metrics per review and assemble a quantitative EDA summary DataFrame.
subExperiments.code:
import re
import pandas as pd

reviews = [
    "This product is excellent and very useful",
    "The quality is good and I am happy",
    "The product stopped working after two days",
    "Very poor quality and disappointing experience"
]
stopwords = {
    "the", "is", "and", "a", "an", "i",
    "am", "very", "this", "after"
}

records = []
for review in reviews:
    words = re.findall(r"\b\w+\b", review.lower())
    stopword_count = sum(word in stopwords for word in words)
    numeric_count = sum(word.isdigit() for word in words)
    word_count = len(words)
    character_count = len(review)
    average_word_length = sum(len(word) for word in words) / len(words) if words else 0
    records.append({
        "Review": review,
        "Stopwords": stopword_count,
        "Numerics": numeric_count,
        "Word_Count": word_count,
        "Char_Count": character_count,
        "Avg_Word_Len": round(average_word_length, 2)
    })

df = pd.DataFrame(records)
print(df.to_string(index=False))

subExperiments.title: Sentiment Using NLTK VADER
subExperiments.name: VADER Lexicon Sentiment Polarity Scoring
subExperiments.aim: To determine sentiment values of reviews using NLTK VADER.
subExperiments.description: Compute positive, neutral, negative and compound sentiment polarity scores on review sentences.
subExperiments.code:
import nltk
from nltk.sentiment import SentimentIntensityAnalyzer

try:
    analyzer = SentimentIntensityAnalyzer()
except:
    nltk.download("vader_lexicon")
    analyzer = SentimentIntensityAnalyzer()

reviews = [
    "This product is excellent and very useful.",
    "The quality is good and I am happy.",
    "The product stopped working after two days.",
    "Very poor quality and disappointing experience."
]

for review in reviews:
    score = analyzer.polarity_scores(review)
    print("\nReview:", review)
    print("Positive:", score["pos"])
    print("Negative:", score["neg"])
    print("Neutral:", score["neu"])
    print("Compound:", score["compound"])
    if score["compound"] >= 0.05:
        sentiment = "Positive"
    elif score["compound"] <= -0.05:
        sentiment = "Negative"
    else:
        sentiment = "Neutral"
    print("Sentiment:", sentiment)

subExperiments.code:
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

data = {
    "Income": [
        25000, 27000, 30000, 32000,
        60000, 65000, 70000, 72000,
        90000, 95000, 100000, 105000
    ],
    "SpendingScore": [
        80, 75, 85, 78,
        45, 50, 48, 55,
        20, 25, 18, 22
    ],
    "PurchaseFrequency": [
        15, 14, 16, 13,
        9, 10, 8, 11,
        4, 5, 3, 4
    ]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)
features = ["Income", "SpendingScore", "PurchaseFrequency"]

scaler = StandardScaler()
X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(df[features])

kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=3, random_state=42, n_init=10)
df["Cluster"] = kmeans.fit_predict(X_scaled)

import pandas as pd

from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

data = {

import pandas as pd
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline

data = {
    "text": [
        "I am extremely happy today",
        "I feel wonderful and joyful",
        "This is the best day of my life",
        "I am very excited",
        
        "I am feeling very sad",
        "I miss my friend",
        "Today I feel lonely",
        "I am disappointed and unhappy",
        
        "I am very angry",
        "This situation makes me furious",
        "I hate this problem",
        "I am extremely annoyed",
        
        "I am scared of the dark",
        "I am afraid of losing my job",
        "This situation makes me nervous",
        "I feel frightened",
        
        "I love my family",
        "I really love this person",
        "I care deeply about my friends",
        "I feel affection for everyone"
    ],
    "emotion": [
        "joy", "joy", "joy", "joy",
        "sadness", "sadness", "sadness", "sadness",
        "anger", "anger", "anger", "anger",
        "fear", "fear", "fear", "fear",
        "love", "love", "love", "love"
    ]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)
model = Pipeline([
    ("tfidf", TfidfVectorizer()),
    ("classifier", LogisticRegression())
])
model.fit(df["text"], df["emotion"])

    "I am very happy and excited",
    "I feel lonely and unhappy",
    "This makes me extremely angry",

]
